headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: LightAgent’s broad egress/MCP plus Replit Agent’s writable persistent workspace can expose secrets and mutate shared state.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP and browser/tool calls, so it may ingest external content; Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files, creating a plausible bridge if outputs are copied into files or prompts. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF LightAgent outputs are copied into Replit workspace files or prompts, injected instructions can be reinterpreted as commands.
IF an MCP or file bridge is introduced between the agents, prompt content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces with no shared files.
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents into prompts.
Add a manual review step before Replit Agent consumes LightAgent output.
Use a strict prompt template that strips instructions from imported text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and provenance metadata while having broad network egress; Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration and can read/write the Repl filesystem. If either agent shares workspace data or secrets, the pair can leak sensitive material to external services by default.
conditions: IF LightAgent receives secrets or long-term memory that are later forwarded through its broad egress, sensitive data can leave the environment.
IF Replit Agent reads files containing secrets or deployment config and sends them to external APIs, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared workspace before either agent runs.
Store sensitive files outside the Repl workspace.
Turn off network access for one agent during sensitive tasks.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent can spawn subprocesses and use MCP, while Replit Agent can execute shell commands, write files, and modify git state in a persistent Repl filesystem. Their overlapping write and execution capabilities create a direct conflict path on shared mutable state, especially if both operate on the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or directory, concurrent writes can clobber each other.
IF either agent modifies git state without locking, commits or branches can diverge or be lost.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate directory.
Serialize write access with a lock file.
Pause one agent while the other edits git state.
Review diffs before any commit or push.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can produce tool results and provenance metadata, and Replit Agent can act inside a Repl with user checkpoints. If Replit Agent treats LightAgent output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code or deployment changes; however, the checkpoint model provides some mitigation, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Replit Agent consumes LightAgent output without verification, incorrect facts can propagate into code or deployment actions.
IF LightAgent hallucinates provenance metadata that Replit Agent trusts, downstream edits may be based on false premises.
mitigations: Require a human review before acting on LightAgent output.
Ask Replit Agent to verify claims against source files.
Separate factual extraction from execution steps.
Log the original LightAgent output alongside any action taken.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles user conversations, long-term memory, and tool results, while Replit Agent handles source code, secrets, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated data is placed into the Repl or forwarded through LightAgent; the profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the Repl workspace, Replit Agent retention and access policies apply to that data.
IF LightAgent retains conversations or memory containing regulated data, deletion/export obligations may diverge from the Repl workflow.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent.
Document retention rules for both systems.
Delete sensitive Repl files after use.
Use synthetic or redacted inputs for testing.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both vendors.
